industry.tan: India FY25: TAN demand 1,319 kt, domestic production 916 kt, imports 422 kt (Emkay initiation, 18-Nov-2025, citing industry data). Demand follows coal and mineral mining and infrastructure blasting; Q2 (monsoon) is the weak quarter and Q4 the strong one (TAN head, call 29-May-2026). Imports (mostly Russia) were disrupted in early 2026 (Russian export ban, plant incidents; India also briefly banned AN exports); Russia lifted its ban in May-2026. New domestic capacity: DFPCL Gopalpur (376 ktpa); Coal India is developing coal-gasification-based AN, technology not yet proven (management, 29-May-2026).
industry.ammonia: Ammonia bulk FOB Middle East ($/t, company presentation): ~$295-330 (Apr-Aug 2025), $430 (Oct-25), $528 (Dec-25), $545 (Mar-26), $707 (Apr-26), $801 (May-26), $777 (Jun-26). ~$600 at end-July (management, Q1 call); Tampa contract $555 for September 2026, a fourth monthly decline (Fertilizer Daily, 10-Sep-2026).
industry.fertInputs: Phosphoric acid bulk CFR India $1,153 (Apr-25) -> $1,292 (Dec-25 to Mar-26) -> $1,360 (Apr-Jun 26); potash CFR $349 -> $383 (Jan-26 onwards) (company presentations). Sulphur costs high (Bensulf volume -44% YoY in Q1FY27).
industry.policy: P&K fertilisers are under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS): the government fixes a per-kg subsidy for N, P, K and S each season and in practice caps farm-gate prices. Kharif 2026 (1-Apr to 30-Sep-2026): outlay Rs41,534 cr, Rs4,317 cr (12%) more than Kharif 2025 (Cabinet, Apr-2026); one report gives N Rs47.32, P Rs52.76, K Rs2.38, S Rs3.16 per kg (only K corroborated). Rabi 2026-27 rates had not been announced by 30-Sep-2026. Urea is under the New Urea/New Investment Policy (DFPCL does not make urea). FY27 budget for NBS and urea subsidy: Rs1,70,799 cr.
industry.monsoon: IMD end-of-season statement (30-Sep-2026): 87% of the long-period average (-12.6%), 'deficient', the weakest since 2015; Central India 97%, Northwest 94%, South Peninsula 76%, East & Northeast 74%. DFPCL's core crop markets (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat) are mostly in Central/West India; management said only 12 of its 44 core districts were likely to be below normal (Q1FY27 presentation).
industry.gas: DFPCL buys gas under a take-or-pay domestic contract and, from May-2026, the 15-year Equinor LNG contract (up to 0.65 MTPA, Henry Hub-linked). Emkay (Nov-2025) estimated gas at ~$11.5/MMBtu under Equinor vs ~$13.5 before, i.e. ~$50 a tonne of ammonia.

moat.evidence: ~40% of India's TAN; the only Indian maker of low-density, high-density and medical-grade AN; west and (from FY27) east coast plants; long ties with Coal India, explosives makers and contractors; B2C/mine-site services 17% of TAN revenue.
Own 500 ktpa ammonia and a 15-year Henry Hub-linked LNG contract cut costs vs buying spot; but the ammonia subsidiary lost Rs257 cr in FY26 and Gopalpur will run on bought ammonia.
TAN, nitric acid, IPA and ammonia follow global prices and imports (Rs45/kg TAN in FY26, Rs70/kg in Q1FY27); fertiliser prices are effectively set by subsidy policy.
Mahadhan is strong in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat; specialty + Croptek ~40% of segment revenue; but segment EBITDA margins of 0-10% show a subsidy-dependent NPK business.
Largest nitric acid maker in South/South-East Asia (62% of India's CNA); 65% of the new Dahej CNA tied up for 20 years.
Ammonia plant cost ~50% over first estimates (Emkay); Gopalpur slipped three times; promoter-linked financing (CCDs, OCDs).

critiques.point: Q1FY27 is a war-time windfall: ammonia at ~$800/t and TAN at Rs70/kg. Ammonia was back near $600 by end-July and Tampa fell for a fourth month in September.
critiques.who: GAM Research; management ('elevated for two to three quarters')

critiques.point: Projects slipped three times (Q4FY26 -> Q1FY27 -> Q2FY27) and costs rose (ammonia ~Rs2,900 cr -> ~Rs4,350 cr; Gopalpur ~Rs2,200 cr -> Rs2,675 cr).
The ammonia subsidiary lost Rs257 cr in FY26 at internal transfer prices; Emkay put its pre-tax ROCE at only ~5-6%.

Promoter-linked financing: a promoter LLP bought Rs300 cr of DMSL CCDs (8% coupon, 12.5% XIRR, put option) partly with money borrowed against pledged DFPCL shares; a promoter company holds Rs151 cr of DFPCL OCDs; MAL committed Rs75 cr to an AIF run by a promoter company.
Fertiliser margins depend on NBS rates keeping up with phosphoric acid and sulphur; Rabi 2026-27 rates were still pending on 30-Sep-2026 and the monsoon was deficient.
Gopalpur is not backward integrated, so it is exposed to imported ammonia prices and logistics; new domestic TAN capacity could pressure prices.
Cash conversion was poor in FY26: operating cash Rs206 cr on EBITDA Rs1,684 cr, as receivables (incl. Rs751 cr of subsidy) and inventory rose.
Pay is high for the size of the company: the CMD drew Rs31.3 cr from the parent in FY26 (4% of consolidated attributable profit), Rs20 cr of it outside salary and commission.
